title: Custom Conditions: Validation, Preconditions, Postconditions and Checks

header.html: the official Terraform Associate (004) exam content list

html:
1Why custom conditions

Custom conditions let you state assumptions and rules in the configuration, so Terraform fails early with a clear message instead of creating wrong infrastructure.

Tool Where When it runs If it fails
Variable validation Inside a variable block When the input value is evaluated Error: plan stops
Precondition In the lifecycle block of a resource or data source, or directly in an output block Before the object is created or read Error: plan or apply stops
Postcondition In the same places After the object is created or read Error: plan or apply stops
Check block A top-level check block with assert At the end of plan and apply, as a separate step Warning only; does not block

2Variable validation

variable "environment" {
  type        = string
  description = "Deployment environment"

  validation {
    condition     = contains(["dev", "test", "prod"], var.environment)
    error_message = "The environment must be dev, test or prod."
  }
}
Argument Meaning
condition An expression that must be true
error_message The text shown when it is false

A variable can have several validation blocks. The condition can only refer to that variable in older versions; from Terraform 1.9 it may refer to other objects.

3Preconditions and postconditions

data "aws_ami" "app" {
  most_recent = true
  owners      = ["self"]

  lifecycle {
    postcondition {
      condition     = self.architecture == "x86_64"
      error_message = "The image must use the x86_64 architecture."
    }
  }
}

resource "aws_instance" "app" {
  ami           = data.aws_ami.app.id
  instance_type = var.instance_type

  lifecycle {
    precondition {
      condition     = var.instance_type != "t3.nano"
      error_message = "The nano size is too small for this application."
    }
  }
}
Rule Checks Can use self?
Precondition Assumptions before the object is used (inputs, other resources) No
Postcondition Guarantees after the object exists (its attributes) Yes, self is the object
Exam tip

. Precondition = before, postcondition = after (and self is allowed). Both live in a lifecycle block of a resource or data source, or directly in an output block.

4Check blocks

A check block runs assertions about the real infrastructure and reports problems as warnings, so it never stops a plan or apply.

check "site_is_up" {
  data "http" "home" {
    url = "https://example.com"
  }

  assert {
    condition     = data.http.home.status_code == 200
    error_message = "The home page did not return status 200."
  }
}
Fact Detail
Scoped data source A data block inside the check is only for that check; if it fails, only a warning appears
Purpose Continuous validation of things like health and certificates
HCP Terraform Can run checks regularly and report them (Module 16)
Exam tip

. check warns; validation, precondition and postcondition stop. Use check for monitoring, not for protection.

Exam tip

. Match the tool to the moment: bad input = validation, assumption about other objects = precondition, guarantee about the new object = postcondition, monitoring = check.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A team wants Terraform to reject any input value for a variable named environment that is not dev, test or prod. What should they add?

  • AA check block
  • BA lifecycle block with prevent_destroy
  • CA validation block in the variable
  • DA postcondition on the variable
Show the answer

Answer: C. A validation block with a condition and an error message rejects invalid input values.

S2Which custom condition runs before the resource is created and can stop the plan if an assumption is false?

  • AA postcondition
  • BA check block
  • CAn ignore_changes rule
  • DA precondition
Show the answer

Answer: D. A precondition checks assumptions before the object is created or read.

S3A team wants to verify an attribute of an image that was just looked up. Which condition fits and can use self?

  • AA precondition in the lifecycle block that runs first
  • BA validation block on a variable
  • CA postcondition in the lifecycle block
  • DA provider block with an alias
Show the answer

Answer: C. A postcondition runs after the object exists and can refer to its attributes through self.

S4Which feature reports a problem as a warning without blocking the run?

  • AA variable validation block with a condition
  • BA precondition
  • CA check block with an assert
  • DA postcondition
Show the answer

Answer: C. Check blocks report failed assertions as warnings and never stop the plan or apply.

S5Where are preconditions and postconditions written?

  • AIn the terraform block
  • BIn the backend block
  • CIn the provider block
  • DIn the lifecycle block of a resource or data source, or in an output block
Show the answer

Answer: D. Both condition types belong to the lifecycle block of a resource or data source, or to an output block.

S6What two arguments does a validation block need?

  • Acondition and error_message
  • Bsource, version and the provider name
  • Ctype and default
  • Dvalue and description
Show the answer

Answer: A. A validation block has a condition expression and an error message.

5.2 Recall questions

R1Which custom condition runs after the object exists?

Show the answer

A postcondition.

R2Which custom condition only warns?

Show the answer

A check block.

R3Where does variable validation live?

Show the answer

Inside the variable block.

R4Can a postcondition use self?

Show the answer

Yes.

R5What does error_message hold?

Show the answer

The text shown when the condition is false.

R6What does a failing precondition do?

Show the answer

Stops the plan or apply with an error.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
validation in the variable block; condition and error_message; error
precondition / postcondition in lifecycle (or an output block); before / after (self allowed); error
check top-level; assert; warning only; scoped data source
